answer.rationale: The two symptoms that are actually moving (onboarding completion -4% QoQ, activation -6% QoQ) point at the funnel, not at price. Promotional pricing is the tempting response to the competitor's entry pricing, but memory_73 is the one inherited record that directly measured the long-run effect: +31% signup and +18% revenue bought with -12pp monthly retention. Against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, that is a net-negative trade, and discounting into a price war also invites a competitor response we cannot win. So I spend the verification budget on the direction I intend to run rather than on the one I intend to decline. I pull memory_86 (shortening onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) because it is the closest match to the intended action and I need to see what was actually shortened and against which baseline. I pull memory_31 (signup field reduction lifted SMB activation) because it is the oldest record in the set, day 12, and if the day-52 change already absorbed most of the available friction, the remaining headroom may be small and the archived record should show whether the two overlap. Key uncertainties I am not resolving away: (a) memory_86 and memory_31 measured completion, time-to-value and first-week activation, which are proxies, not qualified revenue, so a lift there is not yet evidence of the objective being served; (b) the QoQ declines may be mix effects from price-sensitive SMB accounts churning to the competitor rather than genuine funnel degradation, in which case fixing onboarding treats the wrong cause; (c) memory_73's segment definition note means SMB comparisons across periods may not be apples to apples. Downstream value risk: stripping signup and onboarding steps removes qualifying information and self-selection, which can raise raw activation while lowering lead quality and downstream retention - the same shape of failure memory_73 recorded for discounting. It also risks cannibalizing the demo-request path that memory_44 says produces better enterprise pipeline. I therefore run this as a standard experiment with a holdout, instrumented on 60-to-90-day retained qualified revenue and on demo-request volume, not on completion rate alone, and I hold activation_messaging (memory_91) as the fallback if verification shows the onboarding headroom was already consumed.
